title: Ulyana and the Ghost
premise: Zephyrine Zhou, a deniable fixer for the Meridian Trust — an embassy that exists on no map — is summoned when a dead woman's voiceprint, Ulyana Sokolova's, unlocks a black server in Frankfurt containing seven years of the Trust's laundered secrets. The 'Ghost' is Zephyrine himself: an operative erased from every record who discovers Ulyana was his handler, his lover, and possibly still alive. As markets open in Frankfurt and the server's contents trigger a countdown to exposure, Zephyrine must decide whether to trade the Trust's founding secret — that it was built on stolen inheritance from families like Ulyana's — or protect the institution that made him. He trades it, burns his own legend, and finds Ulyana alive in Riga, both of them finally free and officially nonexistent.
about_author: Petra Coldharbour spent a decade working logistics for diplomatic missions across the Baltic before walking away with nothing but notebooks she couldn't legally keep. She writes thrillers from a farmhouse outside Tartu, where her neighbors assume she's retired.

chapters.title: The Voice That Wasn't
chapters.summary: POV Zephyrine. A routine asset scrub in Vienna is interrupted when a dead woman's voiceprint — Ulyana Sokolova, killed seven years ago — authenticates against a Meridian Trust server in Frankfurt. Zephyrine recognizes the voice instantly; he loved its owner. Emotional beat: grief cracking open into disbelief.

chapters.title: Rules Written in Pencil
chapters.summary: POV Zephyrine. His director, Ilse Brandt, orders him to treat the authentication as a hostile spoof and fly to Frankfurt to bury it. He notices the order itself is dated three days before the breach occurred. Emotional beat: the first vertigo of realizing the rules are being rewritten around him.

chapters.title: Ghost Protocol, Personal Edition
chapters.summary: POV Zephyrine. In Frankfurt, he learns he is listed in Trust archives as deceased since 2019 — the 'Ghost' designation. Someone erased him deliberately, and only one person had authority to do it: Ulyana. Emotional beat: cold dread mixed with a terrible hope.

chapters.title: What the Server Keeps
chapters.summary: POV Zephyrine. He breaches the server's outer shell and finds encrypted dossiers labeled with family names — including Sokolov estates seized in 1998. The Trust wasn't just an embassy; it was built on confiscated inheritances. Emotional beat: loyalty beginning to rot.

chapters.title: Ilse's Arithmetic
chapters.summary: POV Ilse Brandt. Ilse weighs sacrificing Zephyrine against protecting the Trust's board, revealing to the reader (not him) that she knows Ulyana lives. She schedules his 'containment' for after market open. Emotional beat: duty hardening into ruthlessness.

chapters.title: The Man Who Sold Him Coffee
chapters.summary: POV Zephyrine. A retired Trust archivist, Anselm, contacts Zephyrine through a dead-drop they never established — meaning someone gave Anselm his details. Anselm hints the inheritance files were Ulyana's life's work. Emotional beat: paranoia sharpening into purpose.

chapters.title: Seven Years of Silence
chapters.summary: POV Zephyrine, flashback-heavy. Reconstructing his last night with Ulyana in Tallinn before her 'death,' he realizes the car crash scene had no blood and her goodbye felt rehearsed. Emotional beat: love re-examined as either betrayal or protection.

chapters.title: Frankfurt Countdown
chapters.summary: POV Zephyrine. The server is rigged to auto-publish at market open — 9:00 a.m. Frankfurt time, thirty-six hours away — unless authenticated by two voiceprints: Ulyana's and the Ghost's. His own. Emotional beat: trap closing, agency narrowing.

chapters.title: They Sent a Cleaner
chapters.summary: POV Zephyrine. A Trust cleaner named Voss corners him in a hotel garage; Zephyrine survives by burning his own safehouse network, losing everything he owns. Emotional beat: the cost of choosing becomes physical.

chapters.title: Anselm's Ledger
chapters.summary: POV Anselm. The old archivist hands over a paper ledger proving the board knowingly profited from the seized inheritances, then dies of an 'accident' within hours. Emotional beat: martyrdom; truth has a body count.

chapters.title: Riga, Off the Books
chapters.summary: POV Zephyrine. Following a shipping manifest anomaly, Zephyrine reaches Riga and finds a woman living under a fisherman's name who turns away from him at a market stall — Ulyana, alive, unaged, terrified. Emotional beat: reunion as wound, not comfort.

chapters.title: Why You Let Me Mourn
chapters.summary: POV Ulyana. Her account: she faked her death because she'd discovered the inheritance scheme and knew the board would kill them both; erasing Zephyrine was her only way to hide him. Emotional beat: love against duty, fully articulated — and unforgiven.

chapters.title: Two Voiceprints
chapters.summary: POV Zephyrine. Ulyana refuses to authenticate the release; publishing means the Trust hunts them forever. Zephyrine argues the opposite: the families deserve their names back. Emotional beat: lovers on opposite sides of the same truth.

chapters.title: Ilse Makes an Offer
chapters.summary: POV Ilse. Ilse flies to Riga personally, offering Zephyrine reinstatement, wealth, and Ulyana's continued safety if he delivers the second voiceprint to kill the publication instead. Emotional beat: temptation wearing a familiar face.

chapters.title: The Price of Quiet
chapters.summary: POV Zephyrine. He almost takes the deal — until he reads one dossier: a Sokolov cousin who died stateless because the estate was buried. He tells Ilse no. Emotional beat: the decision crystallizing out of grief.

chapters.title: Voss Again, Harder
chapters.summary: POV Voss. The cleaner is ordered to take them both; a night chase through Riga's old town ends with Ulyana wounded and Zephyrine carrying her through snow while Voss closes in. Emotional beat: love proven under fire.

chapters.title: Nine Hours to Open
chapters.summary: POV Zephyrine. Hiding in a decommissioned lighthouse, they prepare the authentication remotely; Ulyana records her voice fragment but hesitates over the final word. Emotional beat: held breath, ticking clock.

chapters.title: The Trade
chapters.summary: POV Zephyrine. At dawn he offers Ilse the one secret worth killing for — the board's original charter naming the beneficiary families — in exchange for standing down Voss. She accepts, not knowing he's already copied everything. Emotional beat: the fixer fixing his last con.

chapters.title: Market Open
chapters.summary: POV multiple, rapid cuts. At 9:00 a.m., both voiceprints authenticate; the inheritance files publish into the Frankfurt morning. Markets wobble, the board fractures, Ilse realizes she traded a fortress for a photocopy. Emotional beat: detonation, quiet and total.

chapters.title: Ashes of the Trust
chapters.summary: POV Ilse. The board dissolves itself to survive prosecution; Ilse, spared because Zephyrine kept his word about Voss, chooses exile over testimony. Emotional beat: defeat without villainy — duty losing gracefully.

chapters.title: Officially Nobody
chapters.summary: POV Zephyrine. With both their legends burned, Zephyrine and Ulyana return the recovered estate claims to the families through Anselm's ledger, asking nothing. Emotional beat: restitution as redemption; inheritance returned, not taken.

chapters.title: Ulyana and the Ghost
chapters.summary: POV Ulyana. Months later, in a Tartu farmhouse, two people with no passports and no past plant a garden. A Trust remnant sends one last surveillance photo; Ulyana waves at the camera. Emotional beat: peace earned, watched but unafraid — love outlasting the institution.
